Description: The two-half-day timebox is insufficient for broad solution development
Response or Mitigation: Limit scope to validated assessment, prioritized recommendations, future-state workflow, and implementation roadmap

Description: The team recommends AI before correcting process or data weaknesses
Response or Mitigation: Sequence options from process simplification through standardization, deterministic automation, analytics, then AI
Trigger or Escalation: An AI concept cannot be tied to a validated root cause

Description: Sensitive behavioral-health or incident information is exposed in GitHub or unapproved tools
Response or Mitigation: Use sanitized examples, approved channels, least-necessary access, and no credentials or identifiable records in GitHub

Description: Insufficient baseline data prevents quantified benefits
Response or Mitigation: Document available evidence, label gaps, use ranges only when McCall approves, and recommend baseline measurement
Trigger or Escalation: Volume, time, quality, or delay measures are unavailable

Description: McCall stakeholders with decision authority are unavailable
Response or Mitigation: Confirm one to three working stakeholders and a decision owner before Day 1
Trigger or Escalation: Required decision cannot be made at a phase gate

Description: Tool, integration, procurement, or NextGen constraints make a recommendation infeasible
Response or Mitigation: Validate environment and approvals; state dependencies; provide lower-dependency alternatives
Trigger or Escalation: A recommended approach assumes unverified access or capability

Description: Early AI experimentation is not supported by mature governance or ownership
Response or Mitigation: Define pilot boundaries, human oversight, approval gates, monitoring, acceptable use, and named owners
Trigger or Escalation: No accountable owner or governance route can be named

Description: Recommendations are technically sound but too complex to sustain
Response or Mitigation: Weight readiness and maintainability; use plain language; include phased implementation and training
Trigger or Escalation: McCall cannot explain or own the proposed next step

Response or Mitigation: Use one source of truth, shared definitions, integrated review, and team-lead final consistency check
Trigger or Escalation: Conflicting scope, recommendations, owners, or terminology appear

Description: Incident reports currently move from email to spreadsheets and are manually analyzed
Response or Mitigation: Validate each workflow step, exception, system, and control during discovery
Trigger or Escalation: McCall describes a materially different current state

Description: McCall can provide sanitized examples and approved background materials by September 15
Response or Mitigation: Confirm content, access method, and restrictions during the full-team connector call
Trigger or Escalation: Materials are unavailable or contain restricted information

Description: The Quality Department use case can serve as a pilot for broader AI learning
Response or Mitigation: Treat reuse as a future possibility and avoid assuming direct transfer across functions
Trigger or Escalation: Other functions have materially different data, controls, or workflows

Description: Approved shared folder and relevant resource access
Response or Mitigation: Team lead and McCall establish secure access and confirm the source of truth
Trigger or Escalation: A team member cannot access required non-sensitive materials

Description: McCall input on systems, data, controls, implementation readiness, and desired format
Response or Mitigation: Assign McCall process, technical/control, and implementation contacts
Trigger or Escalation: Required context or review is unavailable

Description: Program Zoom breakout rooms and planning-team support
Response or Mitigation: Use official calendar links and escalate material program issues through the team lead
Trigger or Escalation: Official session or breakout access fails
